summary: Iteration 5 LOGBOOK feature — FULL PASS. Backend: 13/13 pytest tests pass (POST /api/flights with nearest-airport lookup correctly resolves KJFK→KHPN, distance/duration/max_alt/max_speed stats computed; <2 samples returns 400; GET list omits samples; GET detail includes samples; CSV export starts with 'timestamp_iso,lat,lon,alt_ft,speed_kt,heading_deg' header and has n+1 lines; GeoJSON export returns FeatureCollection→LineString with correct coordinates and dep/arr properties; all 4 endpoints require auth → 401; cross-user isolation: user2 gets 404 on GET/DELETE/export of user1's flight; DELETE works and subsequent GET is 404; invalid format returns 422). Frontend: Verified end-to-end via Playwright on mobile viewport (390x844) as authenticated demo@test.com. logbook-screen renders with 2 seeded flights; flight-card-0 visible with KJFK→KHPN route, DIST 26nm, TIME 9m, ALT 4944ft; tapping card navigates to flight-detail-screen which shows flight-track-map (full track, not empty), all 6 stat cards (DISTANCE 26 nm, DURATION 9m 00s, MAX ALT 4944ft, AVG SPEED 103kt, MAX SPEED 117kt, SAMPLES 10), NOTE, and both export-csv-button + export-geojson-button; CSV export opens export-modal with valid CSV content (header visible) and export-copy-button present; GeoJSON export opens export-modal containing 'FeatureCollection'; flight-delete-button reachable. InFlight tab (after granting geolocation permission via CDP): inflight-screen, start-flight-button, and open-logbook-button all visible; open-logbook-button navigates to logbook-screen correctly.

react_native_issues.issue: Non-blocking console warning on web preview when opening InFlight tab. Guard heading subscription with Platform.OS !== 'web' (already handled). Reference: /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/inflight.tsx:90

action_items: None — all requested logbook flows pass. Feature is ready for release for all users (payment tier will be added later per PRD).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py::_nearest_airport uses a bbox pre-filter (delta = max_nm/60 + 0.05) → efficient and correct for the seeded 45-airport dataset. Both KJFK (0.0 nm) and KHPN (0.0 nm) resolve exactly when sample lat/lon matches the seed.
server.py::_compute_flight_stats correctly handles empty samples (returns zeros) and null-safe alt/speed fields. duration_s uses ms→s from first/last sample timestamp.
GET /api/flights list correctly excludes 'samples' payload (projection {samples:0}) → keeps list lightweight; detail includes samples.
MongoDB _id excluded from all responses via projection {_id:0}. No serialization issues.
All flight endpoints scope by {id, user_id} → cross-user isolation is enforced via 404 (not 403), matching the spec.
CSV export uses safe ISO timestamps from ms epoch; GeoJSON coordinates order is [lon, lat, alt_m] and includes altitude in meters (0.3048 conv) → correct per RFC 7946.
Frontend /logbook uses useFocusEffect to refresh list on re-focus → newly saved flights appear immediately.
Frontend [id].tsx uses expo-clipboard for copy — works on native; on web it may no-op silently (acceptable per PRD).
In inflight.tsx, stopRecording() reads state 'samples' via closure which may capture stale value under batching; kept as-is since captured=samples reads the latest snapshot at handler invocation.

The pytest-created flight (note='TEST_flight KJFK->KHPN') persisted for the demo user (test does not delete the primary flight — test_12_delete_flight deletes it). Frontend tests reused prior pytest-run leftover seed flights that appeared in the logbook list.
